title: Hamiltonian Fixed Points Below the Stable Morse Number in Dimension Twenty-Two
coverage:
Read every section (intro, morse, geometry, dynamics, counts) and the first ~120 lines of the handle appendix. Checked these steps:
- Stable lower bound SM ≥ λ: truncation by a ball, cell attachment, Künneth shift, Smith normal form chain bound.
- Smale equality for simply connected manifolds of dimension ≥ 9: classical handle argument, skimmed.
- Homology of the bielliptic surfaces S_2 and S_3: abelianization; Smith normal form of ζ_3−1 is diag(1,3).
- Simultaneous projection of the centres into CP^9: secant and tangent dimensions 2d+1 and 2d, both less than D.
- Integral blow-up formula, with codimensions 7 and 5 giving 6 and 4 shifts.
- Perturbation of the involution: short-period lemma, the identity Φ_ε² = ψ^{2ε}, tangent and normal nondegeneracy, Hamiltonian path built by concatenation.
- Surface Y: weights at the four corners and the half-turn fixing exactly the four exceptional curves.
Recomputed in Python: the 2- and 3-primary profiles a = (2^6) and q = (1,3,4,4,3,1), their convolutions with (1,1) and (1,6,1), and the degreewise maxima. Results: totals 34 and 140, λ(C_m) = 20+488m, λ(M_m) = 80+1968m, 4λ(C_m) = 80+1952m, gap 16m, and ratio m/(5+123m) ≥ 1/128.
Cross-checked against known Floer lower bounds:
- dim H(M_m;F_2) = 80+1792m and dim H(M_m;F_3) = 80+1920m. These are exactly 4·dim H(C_m;F_p), as expected because H(Y) has rank 8 = 4·2.
- The Bai–Xu integral bound with mod-2 grading (minimal Chern number 1, from c_1·E = 2−1) is 80+1920m.
All of these are at most 80+1952m, so the construction does not contradict any established theorem.
main_claim: For every m ≥ 1 there is a simply connected closed Kähler 22-manifold M_m = X_m × Y with SM(M_m) = 80+1968m. It carries a Hamiltonian diffeomorphism with exactly 80+1952m fixed points, all nondegenerate and contractible. The fixed-point count is at most (127/128)·SM, so the stable Morse lower bound fails.
sibling_notes: The family-347 board was empty when I checked. This paper reproduces the companion's (OpenAICompanion) ingredients: the S_2/S_3 bielliptic centres, the integral blow-up formula, the Y half-turn and the involution perturbation (Prop dyn:involution). It also adds the simultaneous projection into CP^9. It proves these ingredients itself rather than citing the companion, so I found no circular dependence.
